claims.title: Live operations and sessions
claims.boundedProposition: Observe current action, model, tokens, cost and an ordered event timeline for a session. Governed work-item and handoff APIs exist and have defined component tests, which were not executed for this measurement; neither is claim-accepted. A goal appears only when the source reports it.
conditions: The session schema records current action, model, tokens, cost and event/timeline data.
A goal is present only when the source reports it.

Governed work-item routes have separate read, write and admin permissions. Work items, dependencies, acceptance criteria, events, leases, decisions and administrative event replay are separate surfaces; the work stream observes their events.

A handoff offer, response, cancellation and deadline execute in one transaction that locks the bound work item and its single work lease, refuses a work item from another workspace lineage, and is idempotent against a stored command receipt.
unpromoted: An accepted task-progress journey: current live-session fields and the work-item APIs are separate source inventories; this measurement does not establish a combined task-progress invariant.
Claim-level acceptance: the work-item and handoff behavior below is source and component-test inventory, not an executed claim-acceptance run.
gaps: The live-operation component test covers ingestion and observable state. It does not bind the published sentence to a user journey, and it was not executed for this measurement.

claims.title: Agent communication and orchestration

owner.implementation: HUB modules/orchestration with HUB modules/sessions workflow ports

claims.boundedProposition: Visualize observed Claude Task, MCP and A2A delegation topology with explicit coverage gaps. Bounded orchestration workflows drive work, runtime, message and handoff controls and read durable acknowledgment state through composition-root ports.
conditions: Coverage is an explicit DTO field, not an implicit promise.
Workflow graph verbs are bounded and enumerated.
Delegation topology is observed, not governed end to end.
Work, runtime, message and handoff controls have separate owners, and durable acknowledgment state is read through its own port. The orchestration and session modules do not depend on each other.

What remains open is that this combined journey has not been executed end to end.
Claim-level acceptance for the public sentence at its route.

claims.title: Simulation sandbox
claims.boundedProposition: Run operator-authored mock scenarios in an isolated ephemeral runner. The composition root constructs gVisor and Firecracker backends only when configuration declares them; OS isolation is attested by that configured backend, never by the mock runner.
conditions: Default behavior is operator-authored mock scenario execution.
Operating-system isolation applies only when the OS runner is configured at composition time; otherwise a configured mock or replay executor runs instead and does not provide it.
Ordered replay depends on an ordered history source.

Attested OS isolation: this source review supplies no executed backend attestation. Backend construction and preflight code are source inventory only.

claims.title: Models, providers and routing
claims.boundedProposition: Define cost, latency, capability or pinned policies and resolve an ordered fallback chain. POST /routing-policies/{id}/execute is deny-closed when execution is not configured. A policy without an execution profile uses the Claude Messages-compatible executor. A policy with an execution profile selects a separate Chat text port on the same route, composed only under explicit development activation with a profile registry and readiness checks.
conditions: Policy resolution produces an ordered candidate chain.
The module always resolves a route and acts only through an executor port. The default executor is unwired, so routing resolves without any provider call until an executor is composed.

The unprofiled executor speaks Claude Messages, directly or through a configured gateway base URL. The profiled Chat text port requires OLIVARES_MODEL_GATEWAY_CHAT_MODE=development_precheck and a profile registry; otherwise profiled execution returns 503. Neither branch establishes a universal provider or model matrix.

The handler applies its stop and scope checks before execution. The unprofiled branch then consults the composed FinOps admission gate. The development Chat branch runs its separate ordered content and routing budget precheck; its declared assurance is non-atomic development precheck, not a qualified hard monetary cap.
unpromoted: A universal provider or model matrix: the Claude Messages protocol establishes one configured route, not a matrix, and this record does not assert that no other product generation path exists.
Centralized key custody: provider key fields are references.
Execution from the console as an accepted journey: the routing panel calls the execute API after explicit confirmation for models:routing:admin users. This source review did not execute that journey.
gaps: No executed provider or version row against a real counterpart exists.

claims.title: FinOps controls that can act
claims.boundedProposition: Apply FinOps admission at composed production gates. Reserve denies when the ledger cannot establish admission; enforcing exhausted budgets deny. The configured inference proxy reserves an estimate before forwarding, then commits observed cost or releases the hold. Legacy CheckBudget retains its fail-open read-error behavior.
conditions: In-process orchestration, voice, evals and model-route gates call Reserve with the deny-on-unreachable posture. Their zero estimate evaluates admission without creating a monetary hold; an unbound evals gate allows until composition binds FinOps.

When its budget gate is enabled, the inference proxy reserves a real estimate before forwarding. Finalization commits measured spend or releases the hold; settlement errors after the effect are logged and the hold expires, rather than undoing the completed effect.

Legacy CheckBudget may return allow with a read error. Session-launch availability is configured separately and may allow an admission refusal; Reserve itself still uses the deny posture. The development Chat route declares a non-atomic precheck assurance, not a qualified hard cap.
Gate decisions carry provider-neutral references and money-free refusal reasons. Internal reservations and inference settlement carry the estimate and actual cost.
unpromoted: A universal hard-cap guarantee across every actuation path, including configured session availability and development Chat execution.
Claim-level acceptance of the reservation, dispatch and settlement journey: source composition and test inventory alone do not establish it.
gaps: The composed Reserve and inference commit/release paths exist at the measured source. This source review supplies no executed claim-level reservation/settlement acceptance artifact.

claims.title: Kill-switch deny gate with dual control
claims.boundedProposition: Stop agent activity through governed stop gates. The hook enforcement point fails closed when stop state cannot be read. The optional inference circuit breaker fails open on a state-read error and relies on the kill-switch as the hard stop. Dual-control recovery is not qualified by this source review.
conditions: The enforcement point fails closed on a stop-state read error.
The circuit breaker returns no denial when it cannot read state and defers to the stop gate.
An operator command surface reports and lists stop state.
unpromoted: Dual-control recovery: no inspected test exercises a dual-control reset or recovery path, so the recovery half of the public sentence is not qualified.
gaps: The end-to-end stop tests are source anchors; no claim-level execution receipt exists and recovery remains unqualified.
